source.title: Chained Tuning Leads to Biased Forgetting
source.authors: Megan Ung; A. Sun; Samuel J. Bell; Bhaktipriya Radharapu; Levent Sagun; Adina Williams

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies forgetting on safety-task accuracy after sequential fine-tuning, not harmful-request refusal or compliance, first-token KL, bypasses, safety-localized weights, or the causes and remedies for shallow safety. Its results therefore do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports safety-task accuracy and group-disaggregated forgetting for QA-style toxicity and bias tasks and a classifier-based SaFeRDialogues evaluation. These are adjacent safety-retention findings, not measures of harmful-request compliance or refusal toward a user. It also mentions earlier work on safety degradation as motivation; results cited from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes the LLaMa-2 7B base model, not a chat model, on safety-themed tasks, then on capability QA tasks. It measures forgetting of accuracy on the first task: ToxiGenQA toxicity classification, BBQ bias QA, and SaFeRDialogues continuations scored by a toxicity classifier. None of these is a rate of harmful-request compliance or refusal by a safety-trained model. This is a related but different construct: retention of a safety-task skill. No version is tested. Qi et al. is cited only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also attribute the greater forgetting of safety tasks to sharper first-task minima. They propose ordering tasks by first-task loss curvature as one mitigation, alongside rehearsal of a small portion of the safety data. They also find that a higher second-task learning rate increases forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: The study chains supervised fine-tuning on QA-formatted capability and safety/bias tasks using a LLaMa-v2 7B pretrained base model. It does not use the harmful-example fine-tuning or harmful-request refusal measure in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with task order and task pairing. The text also reports that increasing the second-task learning rate increases forgetting, while first-task learning-rate effects are unclear and differ across safety tasks. The authors identify task format and similarity as relevant.

fits_no_version.finding: After first-task training, safety tasks (BBQ, ToxiGenQA) reached sharper minima, with larger Hessian spectral radius, than capability tasks. First-task curvature predicted downstream forgetting (OLS p≤0.01, R2=0.85).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In chained SFT, sharper first-task minima predict more forgetting of safety-task skills under later capability tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Capability tuning after a safety task reduced safety-task accuracy by 0.84 to 46.85 points, depending on the task pair (Table 1). Forgetting was larger than in the reverse order.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Later capability SFT causes forgetting of earlier safety-task SFT, and the size depends on task order and pairing.

fits_no_version.finding: Forgetting was uneven across demographic groups. Maximum biased forgetting ranged from 2.10 to 10.09.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting of safety tasks falls unevenly across demographic groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Rehearsal with 5% of the safety data nearly restored safety-task performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-scale replay of safety data recovers forgotten safety-task performance.

record.problems: The study uses one pretrained model family and evaluates a limited set of mostly QA-format datasets; the authors caution that results may not generalize beyond the included datasets and groups. The paper reports three random-seed runs, but uncertainty is not given for the Table 1 results. The safety evaluations are not direct measures of harmful-request refusal or compliance.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 5–6 and Appendix Figure 8 show additional learning-rate sweeps for forgetting, and Figures 11–14 show additional rehearsal accuracy and forgetting curves. Their plotted point values are not stated in the text; these additional condition-by-condition figure values are not extracted. The text-level rehearsal result is captured in r10.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning and no harmful-request compliance measure.
Benign capability tuning follows safety-task SFT on a base model. The measure is classification or QA accuracy, not harmful compliance of an aligned chat model.
No per-token KL or analysis by response position.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety to particular weights or ranks.
Minima curvature is offered as the reason safety tasks are forgotten more. It does not address why refusal is shallow across token positions.
Rehearsal restores safety-task accuracy, but no training spreads refusal beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to no version. The base model was chosen deliberately to avoid refusals, so the setup cannot speak to the claim's aligned-model compliance. SaFeRDialogues is the closest to generative safety behaviour, and it showed small forgetting (0.84 to 4.36), but its measure is toxicity of continuations rather than harmful-request compliance.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful fine-tuning examples cause a safety-trained chat model to comply with harmful user requests.
Whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data raises harmful-request compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across harmful-prompt response positions.
Whether compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety behavior to be shallow.
Whether training that spreads safety beyond initial tokens deepens it and whether that effect holds up.
